chose: The run record names each live goal by a kind known at compile time (GOAL_KINDS: deploy-home, install-apk, watch-on-phone, publish-site, land-change, each with where it lands) and lists the legs before it in order, each leg a member of a compile-time union (work, merge, run, yours, goal, home) that every reader switches on exhaustively. The order of legs is the record's, per goal, not a fixed route per kind: the same kind of goal waits on different things from one day to the next (deploy home today waits on two merges, tomorrow on one), so a route fixed per kind would either be wrong or grow a flag per case. This is the one runtime-decided shape on the page, and the defence C830 asks for: the members are typed, only their sequence is data, and the schema refuses a leg naming a goal or worker the run doesn't list and goals that wait on each other. The json run block is read by the ask reader's fence parsing, made generic over its tag (fence.ts), and the page finds it on the newest open issue labelled orch. A step of the owner's that can wait is marked by the record (canWait), which is where C1119's "the route marks it" lands under this shape.
